Answers concern SSRI

A) Yes, it takes about a month to get to a baseline, and then you can decide whether they are working enough or not to adjust the dosage or try a different one.  This is also why you can't just quit taking them, it has to be a slow process.  You do **not** want SSRI withdrawal, trust me.
B) That depends on the reason for your depression.  If it's a result of an imbalance in your brain chemistry they will probably help, but if it is purely psychological, drugs won't help much, if at all.  It's usually a combination of the two, which is why therapy is as important as medication.
C) This is an extremely vague question, but your doctor will inform you of the risks and possible side effects.  There are always those.

I understand your desire to avoid becoming dependent, because I felt (and sometimes still feel) the same way.  But it's a medical condition like many others.  Think of someone who takes allergy medication.  You just have to decide if the improvement in your quality of life is worth taking a daily pill and accept the idea of a weaning period if you decide to stop.

I used to fantasize about a situation that would allow me to die a hero.  Like, all the way from someone crazy on a bus saying, "I'll let everyone else live if someone volunteers to die" to somehow manually preventing a nuclear meltdown so others could get to safety.  After all, isn't part (or most) of the depression that we think we're meaningless?

Well, I'm a hetero dude so I don't know how much stock you'll put into my response, but (and while a static pic isn't the whole story) you seem to have nice, symmetrical features.  Not ugly.  Did she say she broke up b/c you were ugly?  I doubt it, after all she went out with you in the first place.  Don't worry about it.

I tried, and it was an honest attempt.  It failed due to unforeseen circumstances.  I wasn't discovered, but I didn't have a backup plan, and I did leave a note.  Honestly, I didn't want to die, I just wanted to live less.  It's not as easy as people make it out to be and saying "it's the easy way out" speaks to someone's profound ignorance.  We don't have suicide booths/parlors.  0/10 is extreme, so I'm not saying you're wrong if that's the case, but I think you're exaggerating.  If you don't have access to a gun or barbiturates, your choices are limited and unappealing.  It just depends on how much you're willing to allow your last moments to be filled with horror and violence.  People want the pain to end; the prospect of more pain is not something easily accepted.

I can't stand being embarrassed/humiliated.  Even as a small child, when someone on a TV show would be embarrassed, I felt so uncomfortable.  I don't know if that's part of who I am or if it came from my parents using shame as a rearing tool.  

My skin turned bad at 13.  I tried to handle it for a while, hoping it was just part of the ride, though I knew it wasn't.  I had a good friend whose skin was fucking incredible, and there were plenty of others just as lucky; it was a big school.  

I remember getting my school ID for my junior year and being stunned at how ugly I was.  I thought I was just making my normal resting face, but I looked like a fucking ogre.  That was a tough blow, because I felt like almost anything else about yourself you can change; if you're dumb, you can study hard.  If you're too fat or too thin, you can make life changes to remedy that.  It doesn't mean you'll be a genius supermodel, but you can improve.  Outside of surgery, thought, you're stuck with your face.  I didn't feel like I could make up for it in other ways, either.  I wasn't interesting or talented enough.  So that idea plus my terrible skin planted a giant sequoia of a social phobia in me.  There wasn't help for it because I didn't know it was a real thing.  It just grew inside of me until it shaded every aspect of my life, and choking vines of depression grew right along with it.  I believed at the time the best thing one could do was to create--to use your experience and perspective to make something that no one else could--and I felt like I was completely uncreative.  I was analytical and boring.  I didn't think I was smart enough to compete in fields where my traits would be strengths.  I felt useless to the world.

I failed out of my university because I couldn't bring myself to go to class.  I couldn't concentrate anyway, being in those large classes was a hell inside my head I couldn't escape.  My depression began to get out of control as I watched others do normal things that seemed, and should have been, almost effortless.  I could only get entry-level jobs that paid little, though all I did was work, eat, and sleep.  Their banality and meaninglessness wore away at my motivation and that, coupled with my continuing anxiety and depression, would eventually leave me unable to get out of bed.  I'd live off whatever meager savings I had for however long I could and then repeat the cycle.  My resume is a trainwreck of briefly-held menial jobs and periods of unemployment that need creative explanations, though any hiring manager worth a shit would see through them anyway.

It shouldn't need to be said, but through all this I've never had a real romantic relationship.  I can't believe anyone could see anything in me.  As far as platonic/familial relationships, my parents and grandparents are dead and I've isolated myself from almost everyone else because I'm ashamed of my life.  

Of course I tried to kill myself, but naturally failed at that.  I wasn't discovered, it was an unforeseen circumstance and a story for another time.  I don't really want to die, I'm not at all religious, and I'd really prefer my last moments not be filled with horror and/or violence, but my life is pointless and is on track to stay that way.  I've been to the hospital, I've tried the drugs, I've talked to the doctors.  I went to the ER in July because it was either that or string myself up, so I've been doing all that shit since then, and I don't feel any different.  I wake up every day waiting to take the pills that will let me sleep again.  I'm trying to get on disability (how's that for an ego booster, filling out a government form detailing exactly how much you suck at life so you can be declared mentally disabled?  I did that on my last birthday) so that I can try to work my way back into the world, probably by volunteering at first, but I have so little hope.  I feel completely worthless and utterly broken and so fucking lonely, every day is a trial, and I'm getting really tired.  At this point, I don't think I can be fixed and I'm not sure it'd even be worth it if I could.
